item.text: I’m searching for 2024 evidence on both the pro-stability and anti-stability sides: technocratic macro management, fiscal/debt moves, monetary actions, and whether the policy mix looks sustainable or just reactive. After that I’ll synthesize only the strongest claim-level items.

item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning **no**. Xi’s 2024 macro record includes real stabilization moves, especially property rescue measures, local-debt management, and repeated claims of price-stability support. But the stronger overall pattern is a **reactive, debt-heavy, Party-managed model** with weak monetary independence and continued reliance on off-budget or quasi-fiscal tools rather than a clean long-term stabilization strategy.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Publisher | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| For | The PBOC said it would keep policy “flexible, moderate, precise and effective” and maintain price stability while supporting recovery, which is the clearest official 2024 claim of macro/monetary stabilization intent. | Reuters | 2024-02-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/chinas-central-bank-to-keep-policy-support-for-economy-3297311 | 5B.3 |
| For | The PBOC said it would ensure ample liquidity, support moderate consumer-price recovery, and guard against yuan overshooting, suggesting a genuine effort to preserve monetary and FX stability. | Reuters | 2024-05-10 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/chinas-cenbank-says-it-will-keep-prices-stable-guard-against-yuan-overshooting-risks-3434672 | 5B.3 |
| For | China’s property rescue package cut downpayments and mortgage floors, set up relending for SOE purchases of unsold homes, and financed project completion, which was a real attempt to stabilize households, developers, and unfinished investment. | Reuters | 2024-05-23 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/explainerchinas-latest-property-market-support-package--its-contents-and-whats-at-stake-3455636 | 5B.3, 5B.1 |
| For | IMF staff said China’s authorities were focusing on innovation, green/high-tech sectors, and mitigating property and local-government risks, which supports a reading of trying to preserve broad macro stability rather than pure short-term popularity. | IMF | 2024-05-28 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/05/28/pr24184-china-imf-staff-completes-2024-art-iv-mission | 5B.3, 5B.1 |
| Mixed | IMF’s 2024 Article IV said growth stayed resilient, but the medium-term outlook still weakened without major reforms, with pressure from weak productivity, aging, and debt. That supports the view that Xi was stabilizing the present but not securing durable macro fundamentals. | IMF | 2024-08-02 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/31/pr24295-china-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult | 5B.3, 5B.1 |
| Against | IMF said a neutral fiscal stance would be preferable, debt stabilization requires medium-term fiscal consolidation, and off-budget investment should be reduced. That is strong evidence that the 2024 policy mix had not yet become fiscally responsible or sustainably rebalanced. | IMF | 2024-08-02 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/08/01/peoples-republic-of-china-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-552803 | 5B.3 |
| Against | IMF also said China’s monetary policy framework uses multiple tools with sometimes inconsistent objectives, and that exchange-rate flexibility, fewer quantity controls, and less guidance would improve transmission. That is evidence against strong monetary credibility. | IMF | 2024-08-02 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/08/01/peoples-republic-of-china-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-552803 | 5B.3 |
| Against | Reuters reported that the Party’s debt package to swap hidden local-government debt would improve transparency but also raise official debt and squeeze new project funding, which looks like risk management after years of overborrowing rather than a durable fiscal reset. | Reuters | 2024-11-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/china-unveils-steps-to-tackle-hidden-debt-of-local-governments-2347705/ | 5B.3, 5B.1 |
| Against | Reuters said the de-stocking program for unsold homes was too small to help cash-strapped developers much, which undercuts claims that the property support package meaningfully restored long-term investment conditions. | Reuters | 2024-06-09 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/chinas-home-destocking-push-to-bring-developers-little-cheer-3476774 | 5B.3, 5B.1 |
| Against | Reuters reported the Party created a financial-sector anti-graft committee with political supervision and party-building duties, showing that finance was still being governed through tighter Party control rather than autonomous professional stabilization. | Reuters | 2024-07-24 | https://hk.marketscreener.com/news/latest/China-targets-financial-sector-with-party-led-anti-graft-committee-47453350/ | 5B.3, 5B.2 |

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on policy intent and macro management, but little direct evidence that Xi had a coherent, rules-based commitment to long-term fiscal and monetary credibility.
- The best evidence is indirect: IMF assessments, PBOC statements, and Reuters coverage of specific stabilization measures. The public record does not show a clearly independent central bank or a durable fiscal consolidation program in 2024.
